response:
I read the three files and cross-checked each finding against the code. Here's the plan.

## What the scan actually reports for these three files

The cluster is diagonal, not uniform — no file has all three charge types:

| File | False Identity | Option Bag | Return Shape |
|---|---|---|---|
| `src/index.ts` | `build` (00034), `buildAll` (00041) | — | — |
| `src/rollup.ts` | `getRollupConfig` (00009), `buildStart` (00016) | `getRollupConfig` (00012) | — |
| `src/esbuild/svelte.ts` | — | — | `sveltePlugin` (00035), `setup` (00036), `<anonymous>` (00037) |

Seven findings, but fewer than seven problems. `svelte.ts`'s three return-shape findings are one code region counted at three nesting depths (`sveltePlugin` ⊃ `setup` ⊃ the `onLoad` callback, lines 9–124 / 17–122 / 31–121) — the same three spans that produce its three `large_function` findings. A 124-line file showing six findings has roughly two underlying issues.

---

## Group A — False Identity (`name_behavior_mismatch`)

**`getRollupConfig` — rollup.ts:38 (00009). Real. Fix the body, not the name.**

Line 41 is `setSilent(options.silent)` — a `get*` function mutating the module-level logger singleton from `./log` (fan-in 9, per 00021). The finding also cites `removeFiles`, but that call is at line 79 inside `tsupCleanPlugin.buildStart`, a deferred Rollup hook that runs much later. Half the evidence is wrong; the conclusion stands on `setSilent` alone.

What an agent gets wrong: it calls `getRollupConfig` to inspect or diff a config — a `get*` name invites exactly that — and silently flips global log verbosity for the rest of the worker's life. There's only one call site (`startRollup`, line 217), so this global mutation is load-bearing initialization disguised as a getter.

Proposal: hoist `setSilent(options.silent)` into `startRollup` before the `getRollupConfig` call. Lift `tsupCleanPlugin` and `ignoreFiles` (lines 75–91) to module scope as factories taking `{clean, outDir}`, so the returned config is data rather than closures capturing all of `options`.

**`buildStart` — rollup.ts:77 (00016). Decline — false positive.**

This is a Rollup plugin hook. The name is Rollup's plugin interface, not a choice, and `removeFiles` is precisely what the hook exists to do. Renaming breaks the plugin. The prefix heuristic can't tell that a `build*` method on an object literal inside a `plugins: []` array is a framework contract. Suppress it rather than "fixing" it.

**`build` — index.ts:167 (00034). Reframe — don't rename.**

`build` is the package's exported public API. Renaming is a breaking change for every consumer, and "callers may treat this as pure" is not a plausible failure for a bundler's `build`. The detector's cited side effects (`createLogger`, `removeFiles`) also understate things: `build` also sets `process.exitCode` (line 360), spawns child processes (355), starts a chokidar watcher (406), and **never resolves in watch mode**. That last one is the real hazard, and the fix is a doc comment on the export plus the structural split below — not a name.

**`buildAll` — index.ts:291 (00041). Real, and the name is genuinely the problem.**

A 75-line closure that deletes the output directory (line 307) before doing anything else. Two specific traps:

- "All" means all *formats*, not all *tasks*. Declaration files come from a separate `dtsTask` running in a separate worker process, joined at line 455. An agent adding a new output format will wire it into `buildAll` and be confused when dts doesn't follow — or worse, will assume `buildAll` covers dts and remove the parallel task.
- It's referenced at line 285 by `debouncedBuildAll` *before* its own `const` declaration at 291. That only works because `debouncePromise` defers the call past the TDZ. Any agent that hoists, reorders, or extracts these closures gets a `ReferenceError` at runtime, not at compile time.

Proposal: rename to `runFormatBuilds`; extract the clean block (298–309) into `cleanOutDir(options, logger)` called from the same place, so "does this delete my dist?" is answerable at the call site; move the declaration above `debouncedBuildAll` to drop the TDZ dependence.

---

## Group B — Option Bag Junk Drawer (`getRollupConfig`, rollup.ts:38, 00012)

The finding says "implicit shape," but the parameter *is* typed — `options: NormalizedOptions`. The problem is width, not absence. `NormalizedOptions` is `Omit<MarkRequired<Options, …>>` over a 279-line `Options` type; the signature claims this function may touch anything tsup can be configured with, when it reads eleven fields (`silent`, `dts`, `entry`, `outDir`, `format`, `external`, `clean`, `cjsInterop`, `tsconfig`, `outExtension`, plus `watch` in the caller).

**This is the sharpest finding in the cluster, and it's hiding a live defect.**

`getRollupConfig` runs in a worker. Options arrive via `postMessage` (rollup.ts:230–238), and index.ts:222–238 explicitly strips every non-cloneable field on the way in — including `outExtension: undefined` at line 237, under the comment `// functions cannot be cloned`.

But rollup.ts:141 reads:

```ts
options.outExtension?.({ format, options, pkgType: pkg.type }).dts ||
  defaultOutExtension({ format, pkgType: pkg.type }).dts
```

`options.outExtension` is *always* undefined on this path by construction. The optional chain swallows it and silently falls through to the default. A user-supplied `outExtension` returning `{ dts: … }` is honoured for JS output and quietly ignored for declaration files. TypeScript can't catch it because `NormalizedOptions` says the function is there — the type describes the pre-worker shape, and nothing describes the post-clone shape.

The one test that covers this (`test/index.test.ts:640`, "custom output extension") returns only `{ js: … }` and never runs with `--dts` — which is also why it shows up as a weak-signal finding (00084).

Proposal, in order:

1. `type DtsBuildOptions = Pick<NormalizedOptions, 'entry'|'outDir'|'format'|'external'|'clean'|'cjsInterop'|'silent'|'tsconfig'|'dts'>` — note `outExtension` is deliberately absent.
2. Change `getRollupConfig(options: DtsBuildOptions)`. The compiler now flags line 141 as an error instead of silently no-op'ing it. Decide there whether to fix the feature (send the resolved extension string across the boundary, since strings clone fine) or delete the dead branch — but decide it explicitly.
3. Write the projection as a named function at the `postMessage` site so the worker boundary has one place that says what survives it.

Step 1–2 are mechanical and compiler-verified. `runEsbuild` has the same disease at 38 property reads (00040) — same pattern, much larger job, keep it in a separate change.

---

## Group C — Return Shape Roulette (svelte.ts, 00035/36/37)

The suggested fix — "pick one return shape; use a discriminated union" — is the wrong prescription here, and an agent that follows it literally will break the plugin. The "6 object-literal return shapes" belong to five *different* callbacks that the detector rolls up because they're lexically nested inside `sveltePlugin`:

| Line | Shape | Contract owner |
|---|---|---|
| 22–28 | `{path, namespace}` | esbuild `OnResolveResult` |
| 37–39 | `{errors}` | esbuild `OnLoadResult` |
| 57 | `{text, location}` | esbuild `PartialMessage` |
| 79 / 92–95 | `{code}` / `{code, map}` | svelte-preprocess `Processed` |
| 117 / 119 | `{contents, warnings}` / `{errors}` | esbuild `OnLoadResult` |

Every shape is dictated by an external API. You can't unify them and shouldn't try. But the underlying concern — agents inferring the wrong contract — is valid, and there's a real bug sitting exactly where the detector is pointing:

`convertMessage` (line 43) takes `({message, start, end}: any)`. It's called at line 119 on a caught `error` of type `unknown`. If anything other than a Svelte compile error escapes the `try` — a `TypeError` from the preprocessor, a failure from the `localRequire` shim — it reads `.message`/`.start`/`.end` off an object that has none, `location` stays undefined, and esbuild receives `{errors: [{text: undefined}]}`. An empty error box, original stack destroyed. Same class as the `swallowed_error` findings elsewhere in this repo, arrived at from a different direction.

`convertMessage` also closes over `source` and `filename` (lines 46, 50) that are declared *below* it at 61–62 — TDZ-safe only because of call ordering, same trap as `buildAll`.

Proposal:

- Annotate the callbacks with esbuild's own exported types: `(args): OnResolveResult` on line 21, `async (args): Promise<OnLoadResult>` on line 31. This satisfies the detector's literal complaint (no explicit return type) *and* makes the compiler check each shape against the real contract — which is stronger than a hand-rolled union.
- Give `convertMessage` a real signature: `(err: unknown, source: string, filename: string): PartialMessage`, with a narrowing guard and a `{ text: String(err) }` fallback so a non-Svelte throw still produces a readable error.
- Lift it to module scope. That removes the TDZ coupling, and since it's the largest block in the 91-line anonymous callback, it also takes a good chunk out of findings 00046/00049/00070 for free.
- Type the `script` preprocessor hook's return as svelte-preprocess's `Processed`.

---

## What an agent extending these modules gets wrong today, in one list

1. Calls `getRollupConfig` to inspect a config and silently mutates global log state.
2. Adds an output format to `buildAll` and can't work out why declaration files don't follow — they're built by a different task in a different process.
3. Reorders or extracts the closures in `mainTasks` or the `onLoad` body and gets a runtime `ReferenceError` that the compiler never warned about.
4. Reads `NormalizedOptions` on `getRollupConfig`, `runEsbuild`, and `main`, sees the same god-type on all three, and adds handling in the wrong layer — or in two layers.
5. Trusts `options.outExtension` in the dts worker because the type says it's there. It never is.
6. Renames `buildStart` to satisfy the linter and breaks the Rollup plugin.
7. Collapses the esbuild callback returns into a discriminated union to satisfy 00035 and breaks the esbuild plugin.

Items 6 and 7 are cases where following the tool's `fix_shape` verbatim causes the damage — worth noting given these are agent-risk detectors.

## Suggested sequencing

1. **Type projection at the worker boundary** (Group B). Highest value, mechanical, compiler-verified, and it surfaces the `outExtension` defect rather than papering over it.
2. **Explicit return types in `svelte.ts`** (Group C) + lift `convertMessage`. No behaviour change except the error-path fix; clears six findings.
3. **`setSilent` hoist and `buildAll` rename** (Group A). Small, but touches `src/index.ts` — fan-out 17, flagged load-bearing by 00074. Do it alone, not stacked on the others.
4. **Suppress 00016**, and add a doc comment to `build` covering watch-mode non-resolution and `process.exitCode`.

Nothing here needs `Promise.all` restructuring or file splits — the `large_function`/`large_file` findings on these paths largely dissolve as a side effect of steps 2 and 3.

I made no edits; say the word and I'll start with step 1.
